archetypes.name: Short (Hertzian) dipole
archetypes.summary: Electrically short centre-fed dipole with an assumed triangular current distribution.

parameters.name: electrical length
parameters.description: total length as a fraction of the free-space wavelength

analysis.notes: Rr = 20*pi^2*(L/lambda)^2 for the triangular current distribution a real short dipole carries (Balanis 4-37). This is the practical value.

Rr = 80*pi^2*(L/lambda)^2, the uniform-current infinitesimal dipole (Balanis 4-19). Four times the triangular value, because Rr scales with the square of the effective length (L/2 triangular, L uniform). Reached in practice only by capacitive top loading - see top_loaded_monopole.
exact for sin^2 theta
L/2 for the triangular distribution; L for a uniform current
exact for the sin^2 pattern

validity: L < 0.1*lambda, beyond which the current is no longer approximately linear
thin wire, radius << L
Rr excludes ohmic and ground loss; a short dipole's efficiency is usually loss-dominated

known_cases.source: Rr = 20*pi^2*(0.01)^2 = 0.019739 ohm triangular, 80*pi^2*(0.01)^2 = 0.078957 ohm uniform; D = 1.5 = 1.761 dBi. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., eqs. 4-19 and 4-37
quadratic scaling check: 25x the 0.01 case. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4

archetypes.name: Half-wave dipole
archetypes.summary: The canonical centre-fed dipole of exactly half a wavelength; the reference antenna for dBd.

parameters.name: wire radius
parameters.description: conductor radius; only the reactance depends on it

synthesis.notes: exactly lambda/2; see resonant_dipole for the length that actually resonates

analysis.notes: exact Balanis 4-70; 73.08 ohm with eta0 = 376.73 (textbooks quoting 73.13 use 120*pi)
exact Balanis 4-79; +42.5 ohm at exactly lambda/2, which is why real dipoles are cut short
numerically integrated; see otahub.core.pattern.finite_dipole(0.5)
numerically integrated
l_e = lambda/pi for a half-wave dipole

validity: free space, no ground plane or nearby structure
thin wire: the reactance formula assumes aw << L
at exactly lambda/2 the antenna is NOT resonant (X = +42.5 ohm)

known_cases.source: Balanis: Rr = 73.13 ohm, X = +42.5 ohm, D = 1.643 (2.15 dBi) at L = lambda/2
lambda/2 at 2.4 GHz = 62.44 mm

archetypes.name: Resonant dipole (thickness corrected)
archetypes.summary: A dipole shortened from lambda/2 so that its input reactance is zero at f0.

synthesis.notes: Quadratic fit to the exact zero of Balanis 4-79, computed over a/lambda = 1e-5..1e-2 (L/d = 50 to 50000). Max error 0.42% of a wavelength across that range. Outside it, solve X(L) = 0 directly.

analysis.notes: 55-68 ohm across practical thicknesses, always below the 73 ohm lambda/2 value
zero by construction, to within the fit error
resistive-only estimate, valid because X ~ 0 at resonance
the 1-2% shortening barely changes the pattern

validity: 1e-5 < aw/lambda < 1e-2; outside this the length fit is untested
thin-wire theory: no insulation, no end capacitance from hardware
free space; height above ground shifts resonance by more than this correction

known_cases.source: exact zero of Balanis 4-79 at a/lambda = 1e-4 is L = 0.48463 lambda Reactance is checked with an absolute tolerance of 6 ohm: the length fit carries 0.42% error, which maps to a few ohm of residual reactance against a 66 ohm radiation resistance (VSWR < 1.1).
exact zero at a/lambda = 1e-3 is L = 0.47751 lambda
exact zero at a/lambda = 1e-2 is L = 0.45738 lambda, Rr = 55.74 ohm

references: resonant lengths computed from the exact reactance by root-finding

archetypes.name: Quarter-wave monopole over a ground plane
archetypes.summary: Half a dipole over an infinite perfect ground plane; image theory doubles the directivity.

synthesis.notes: the equivalent dipole formed with the image

analysis.notes: half the dipole value: same radiated power into half the space. 36.54 ohm.
+21.26 ohm at exactly lambda/4
twice the dipole: radiation confined to the upper hemisphere
5.16 dBi
elevation half-power beamwidth measured from the horizon upward

validity: infinite, perfectly conducting ground plane
a finite ground plane raises Rin and tilts the pattern upward; below about 0.25*lambda radius the effect is severe
real earth is lossy: ground loss often exceeds radiation resistance at HF

known_cases.source: Half the half-wave dipole impedance: 36.5 + j21.25 ohm; D = 5.15 dBi. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4 Ch. 4.7 (image theory)

archetypes.name: Folded dipole
archetypes.summary: Two parallel half-wave conductors joined at the ends; steps the impedance up by N^2.

synthesis.notes: slightly short of lambda/2, as for any real dipole
typical practical spacing, 0.01-0.05 lambda; must stay << lambda for the transmission-line mode to be non-radiating

analysis.notes: equal-diameter conductors carry equal currents, so the feed sees N^2 times the single-dipole impedance
292.3 ohm for the standard two-conductor case, the classic 300 ohm twin-lead match
pattern is indistinguishable from a plain dipole
roughly twice a plain thin dipole's, from the lower effective Q of the two-conductor structure. Indicative: the true figure depends on d_sep/aw.

validity: d_sep << lambda so the transmission-line mode does not radiate
equal conductor diameters; unequal diameters give a step ratio between 1 and N^2
bandwidth figure is indicative, not a closed-form result

known_cases.source: 4 x 73.08 = 292.3 ohm, the standard folded-dipole result. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4
N^2 scaling: three-wire folded dipole is 9 x 73.08. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4 Ch. 9.5

archetypes.name: Biconical antenna
archetypes.summary: Two opposed cones; a travelling-wave structure whose impedance is set by the cone angle.

parameters.name: cone half angle
parameters.description: half angle measured from the axis; 30 deg = 0.5236 rad

synthesis.notes: slant length of about lambda/4 at the lowest frequency sets the low-end cutoff

analysis.notes: Zc = (eta0/pi)*ln(cot(theta_h/4)), exact for the INFINITE biconical (Balanis 10-20). A finite cone departs from this near the low-frequency end.
close to a dipole for narrow cones; widens as theta_h grows. Indicative only.
Indicative: practical finite biconicals reach roughly a decade of usable VSWR bandwidth. Not a closed-form result.

validity: characteristic impedance is exact only for an infinite structure
theta_h between about 1 and 60 degrees
directivity and bandwidth entries are indicative, not derived

known_cases.source: theta_h = 30 deg: Zc = (eta0/pi)*ln(cot(7.5 deg)) = 243.2 ohm. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4
theta_h = 10 deg: theta_h/4 = 2.5 deg, cot = 22.9038, Zc = (eta0/pi)*ln(22.9038) = 375.50 ohm. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 10.3

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4 Ch. 10.3 (eq. 10-20)

archetypes.name: Centre-fed dipole of arbitrary length
archetypes.summary: Sinusoidal-current dipole from 0.05 to 1.2 lambda, solved exactly in Si/Ci rather than by interpolation.

parameters.name: electrical length
parameters.description: tip-to-tip length as a fraction of the free-space wavelength

analysis.notes: Balanis 4-70, referred to the current maximum. Verified against direct numerical integration of the pattern at 0.1, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 and 1.25 lambda.

Referred to the FEED current, which for L != lambda/2 differs from the current maximum by sin(kL/2). The two coincide only at the half-wave point. Diverges as L approaches lambda, where the idealised sinusoid puts a current null at the feed; a real full-wave dipole shows a few kilohms, not infinity.
Balanis 4-79; the only place wire radius enters
|F| at theta = 90 deg. Broadside remains the pattern maximum up to about 1.2 lambda, confirmed by scanning |F(theta)| on a 200k-point grid.
D = eta*|F|^2/(pi*Rm), exact for L <= 1.2 lambda. Reproduces 1.5010 at 0.1 lambda, 1.6409 at 0.5 and 2.4110 at 1.0 - the textbook full-wave dipole value.
dBd: how much this length buys over a half-wave dipole

validity: 0.05 < L/lambda < 1.2; above ~1.25 lambda the main beam splits and broadside is no longer the maximum
assumed sinusoidal current, which is the standard thin-wire idealisation
input resistance is unusable within a few percent of L = lambda, where the model puts a current null at the feed
no ground plane, no loss

known_cases.source: The half-wave dipole: 73.08 ohm and D = 1.641. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.6
Full-wave dipole: Rr = 199 ohm referred to the current maximum, D = 2.41. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Table 4.1 / Fig. 4.13
Quarter-wave dipole, independently reproduced by numerical integration of the sinusoidal-current pattern. The factor-of-two gap between the two resistances is the sin^2(kL/2) referral.

references: Numerically cross-checked against quadrature of the exact pattern integral

archetypes.name: Horizontal dipole over a ground plane
archetypes.summary: Horizontal half-wave dipole at height h above a perfect conductor, solved by image theory with exact mutual impedance.

parameters.name: height above ground
parameters.description: height as a fraction of the free-space wavelength

synthesis.notes: the image sits as far below the plane as the dipole sits above it, with reversed current

analysis.notes: isolated-dipole value, Balanis 4-70

analysis.expr: (eta0/(4*pi))*(2*Ci(k0*d_image) - Ci(k0*(sqrt(d_image**2 + L**2) + L)) - Ci(k0*(sqrt(d_image**2 + L**2) - L)))
analysis.notes: Balanis 8-72a for parallel side-by-side half-wave dipoles. Reproduces the textbook -12.5 ohm at d = lambda/2.

analysis.expr: -(eta0/(4*pi))*(2*Si(k0*d_image) - Si(k0*(sqrt(d_image**2 + L**2) + L)) - Si(k0*(sqrt(d_image**2 + L**2) - L)))
analysis.notes: Balanis 8-72b. Reproduces -29.9 ohm at d = lambda/2.
MINUS, because the image current is reversed. This is why a low horizontal dipole feeds at 30 ohm rather than 73.
field ratio relative to the same current in free space; 2.0 at h = lambda/4
Directivity straight up. Reproduced to five digits by direct numerical integration over the upper hemisphere.
Elevation of the lowest array-factor maximum, where k*h*cos(theta) = pi/2. Pinned at 90 deg (zenith) for h <= lambda/4; 30 deg at h = lambda/2.
the same dipole with no ground present, for comparison

validity: perfectly conducting, infinite ground plane; real earth is lossier and tilts the low-angle lobe
zenith is the pattern peak only for h <= lambda/4 and at h = lambda/4 + n*lambda/2; elsewhere read first_lobe_elevation_deg
mutual impedance formula is the half-wave side-by-side result, so it is exact only near L = lambda/2
no conductor loss: at h = lambda/8 the feed resistance falls to 32 ohm and loss matters more than these figures suggest

known_cases.source: Mutual impedance of parallel half-wave dipoles at d = 0.5 lambda is -12.5 - j29.9 ohm (Balanis 4th ed. Fig. 8.21). Peak directivity independently confirmed at 5.6034 (7.485 dBi) by hemisphere integration.

A dipole one eighth of a wavelength up has HIGHER zenith directivity than one at a quarter wave (8.70 vs 7.48 dBi), because the image adds in phase and the feed resistance collapses to 32 ohm. Confirmed by hemisphere integration.
cos(theta) = lambda/(4h) = 0.5 puts the lobe at 60 deg from zenith, i.e. 30 deg elevation - the standard half-wave-high dipole result

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.7 (image theory) and Ch. 8.6 (eqs. 8-72)
Numerically cross-checked by integrating the full pattern over the upper hemisphere

archetypes.name: Capacitively top-loaded short monopole
archetypes.summary: Electrically short vertical with a top hat that flattens the current taper, raising radiation resistance by up to four times.

parameters.name: top/base current ratio
parameters.description: 0 = bare whip (triangular current), 1 = ideal hat (uniform current). 0.5-0.8 is typical for a real hat.

synthesis.notes: exact for a linear current taper: the area under the taper divided by the base current

analysis.notes: Rr = 160*pi^2*(h_eff/lambda)^2 for a monopole over a perfect ground plane - half the uniform-current dipole of length 2*h_eff. Collapses to the classic 40*pi^2*(h/lambda)^2 when beta_top = 0.
the same rod with no hat, for comparison
up to 6.02 dB at beta_top = 1, where the current is fully uniform

Exact for the linear taper: integral of |I/I0|^2 along the rod is h*(1+beta+beta^2)/3, which is h/3 for a bare whip and h when fully loaded. Hat and ground-system loss are NOT included and usually dominate at HF.
exactly 3.0 for any short vertical over an infinite perfect ground plane - twice the free-space dipole's 1.5
Isolated thin disc, C = 8*eps0*a. A hat close to ground reads higher. Sizing aid only: this spec does not derive beta_top from the hat size.
Chu/McLean lower bound for a linearly polarised antenna inside a sphere of radius h. No amount of top loading beats this.

validity: h < 0.1*lambda, where the linear current taper is a good description
perfect infinite ground plane; a real radial ground system adds loss resistance that often exceeds Rr
beta_top is an input, not a prediction - relating hat size to beta_top needs a numerical solve this spec does not attempt
hat and ground loss excluded, so radiation_efficiency is an upper bound

known_cases.source: With no hat the model must return the textbook short-monopole value 40*pi^2*(h/lambda)^2 = 0.987 ohm. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.8
beta_top = 0 is the bare whip, so the loading gain must be exactly 0 dB. Expectations of zero need tol_abs.
A fully uniform current quadruples Rr, exactly 6.02 dB. Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., eqs. 4-19 and 4-37
beta = 0.6 gives h_eff/h = 0.8, so Rr = 160*pi^2*0.04^2 = 2.527 ohm. Directivity of any short vertical over perfect ground is 3.0 = 4.771 dBi.

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.8 (monopoles) and eqs. 4-19, 4-37
McLean, A re-examination of the fundamental limits on the radiation Q, IEEE T-AP 44(5), 1996

archetypes.name: Inductively loaded short monopole
archetypes.summary: Short whip resonated by a series loading coil, with the efficiency penalty the coil brings.

parameters.name: top/base current ratio
parameters.description: 0 for a base-loaded bare whip; centre loading or a hat raises it

parameters.name: loading coil Q
parameters.description: 150-300 for a well-made air-core coil; under 100 for a compact loading inductor

parameters.name: ground system resistance
parameters.description: loss of the radial or vehicle-body ground; 0 for an ideal plane

synthesis.notes: the image makes the monopole behave as a dipole of length 2h, at half the impedance

analysis.notes: Half the exact Balanis 4-79 dipole reactance, because the monopole sees half the dipole's impedance. Strongly capacitive: a 1.5 m whip at 10 MHz shows about -j111 ohm.
series inductance that cancels the antenna reactance at f0
R = |X|/Q. This is the dominant loss in most loaded whips, and it grows as the antenna shortens - exactly where Rr is collapsing.
what the transmitter sees at resonance. A convenient 50 ohm here is usually bad news: it means loss, not radiation.

validity: h < 0.1*lambda
single lumped coil, assumed lossless apart from its Q; distributed loading behaves better
coil placement is captured only through beta_top, not modelled directly
ground loss is an input, and at HF it commonly exceeds every other term

known_cases.source: A 1.5 m whip at 10 MHz: Rr = 0.987 ohm from the short-monopole formula, and -j111 ohm from the exact Balanis 4-79 reactance halved. The two formulas are independent, and the exact input resistance 0.9994 ohm confirms the 0.987 approximation to 1.3%.
L = |X|/omega = 111.03/(2*pi*10e6) = 1.77 uH; R_coil = |X|/Q = 0.555 ohm, over half the radiation resistance. This is why short loaded whips are inefficient.

references: ARRL Antenna Book, mobile and shortened-vertical chapters, for the coil-Q and ground-loss ranges

archetypes.name: Turnstile (crossed dipoles in quadrature)
archetypes.summary: Two crossed half-wave dipoles fed 90 degrees apart: circular polarisation on axis, near-omnidirectional in the plane of the elements.

synthesis.notes: A quarter-wave of line in one feed is the classic way to get the 90 degrees. It is narrowband - the axial ratio degrades either side of f0 - and the line's electrical length must account for its own velocity factor.

analysis.notes: one element in isolation; the crossed elements barely couple
Equal to a SINGLE dipole's directivity. Splitting the power two ways is exactly offset by the two orthogonal polarisations adding on axis - confirmed by numerical integration.
Along either element axis, where only the other dipole radiates: exactly 3 dB below the axial value, about -0.86 dBi for half-wave elements.
The 45-degree azimuth, where the pattern dips. Powers add because the two polarisations are orthogonal, so there is no interference term.
About 1.03 dB for exactly half-wave elements - the turnstile is near-omnidirectional but not perfectly so
perfect circular polarisation on axis, by symmetry, when the feed is exactly in quadrature
each element behaves essentially as an isolated dipole

validity: mutual coupling between the crossed elements is neglected; it is genuinely small because each sits in the other's null
exact quadrature assumed - the quarter-wave line achieves it at one frequency only
free space, no reflector; a turnstile over a ground plane or with a crossed reflector behaves quite differently
circular polarisation holds only on the axis normal to both elements; the element plane is linearly polarised

known_cases.source: Numerical integration over the full sphere of U = |Fx|^2 + |Fy|^2 gives D = 1.64092 on axis and 0.82046 along an element - identical to a single dipole on axis, exactly 3 dB down in the element plane.
The 45-degree azimuth minimum is 0.64702 (-1.891 dBi), giving 1.03 dB of ripple. Independently reproduced on a 1201 x 2402 angular grid.
symmetry: equal-amplitude orthogonal fields in exact quadrature are circular by construction

references: Balanis, Antenna Theory 4th ed., Ch. 4.6 for the element, Ch. 6 for polarisation
Numerically cross-checked by spherical integration of the summed-power pattern
